body.title: Send invoice throws TypeError in sendInvoice on /invoices/new
body.summary: The user opened a new invoice, entered a customer and amount, saved a draft, and clicked Send invoice. The send action threw a TypeError in sendInvoice, and the user then rage-clicked the Send invoice button with no successful send shown in the timeline.
body.expected: Clicking Send invoice sends the invoice without an error.
body.actual: Clicking Send invoice raises TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') at sendInvoice (InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21). The user then rage-clicked #send-invoice five times.

evidence.note: Primary failure: uncaught TypeError in sendInvoice at InvoiceSendButton.tsx:48:21 when Send invoice is clicked.
Same TypeError logged to the console, confirming the failure at the moment of sending.
Rage click x5 on #send-invoice shows the user repeatedly retrying a button that does not complete the send.

body.suspected_cause: Likely sendInvoice reads the .id property of a value that is undefined at send time, such as a customer or invoice reference not populated after the draft is saved.
body.signature: exc:TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'id') @ InvoiceSendButton.tsx

body.title: Send reminder fails with 500 (reported by [email])
body.summary: The user opened invoice inv_8812 and clicked Send reminder, then clicked it again a few seconds later. Both attempts returned a 500 internal_error from the reminders endpoint and showed a generic 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' message.
body.expected: Clicking Send reminder sends the payment reminder for the invoice without error.
body.actual: The POST /api/invoices/inv_8812/reminders request returns 500 (internal_error) and the user sees 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' Retrying produces the same result.

evidence.note: Primary failure: the reminders endpoint returns 500 internal_error on the first send attempt.
The user sees a generic error message, so the failure is visible and the reminder is not sent.
The same 500 internal_error repeats on the second attempt, so retrying does not help.

body.suspected_cause: Likely a server-side exception in the reminders endpoint for this invoice, since the request fails quickly (about 400 ms) with a generic internal_error both times.

body.title: AR aging report times out with 504 from /api/reports/aging
body.summary: The user opened the reports page and clicked AR aging (#aging-report). The aging request returned a 504 gateway_timeout after 30012 ms, and the user saw a 'taking too long' message and rage-clicked the report link.
body.expected: The AR aging report loads and displays.
body.actual: The aging request returns 504 (gateway_timeout) after about 30 seconds, and the user sees 'This report is taking too long. Try a shorter range.' The user rage-clicked the link several times.

evidence.note: GET /api/reports/aging?range=… returned 504 after 30012 ms, which is the primary failure.
Four rapid clicks on #aging-report show the user was waiting on a non-responsive report.
The user was shown a timeout message suggesting a shorter range, confirming the failure reached the UI.

body.suspected_cause: The aging report query likely runs longer than the 30-second gateway timeout for the requested range.

body.title: Payments page fails to load: chunk 812 returns 404 after deploy
body.summary: The user opened the dashboard and clicked Payments in the navigation, which opened /payments at 00:01. The page failed to load because the chunk request for 812.3f9a1c.chunk.js returned 404, and the user saw "Page failed to load."
body.expected: The /payments page loads and shows its content.
body.actual: The chunk GET /static/js/812.3f9a1c.chunk.js returned 404, a ChunkLoadError was thrown, and the user saw "Page failed to load."

evidence.note: The chunk request returned 404, which is the primary failure.
The ChunkLoadError confirms the page's JavaScript chunk could not be loaded.
The user-facing message shows the page failed to load.

body.suspected_cause: A likely stale or missing build asset after the 2026.10.27-1 deploy, where clients still reference chunk 812.3f9a1c that the server no longer serves.

body.body: +1 from another session (Chrome 141, app 2026.10.27-2): POST /api/invoices/inv_7731/pdf -> 500 in 2800 ms (pdf_render_failed) at [00:02]. Replay: https://us.posthog.com/project/102/replay/rec_07_pdf_dup?t=0

body.title: CSV export of customers fails with 500 error on /customers page
body.summary: The user opened the customers page and clicked Export CSV. The export request to /api/customers/export returned a 500 error, and the user saw an "Export failed." message.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Open the customers page (/customers with a search query).

body.expected: The customer CSV export completes and the file downloads.
body.actual: The export request returns a 500 error and the user sees "Export failed."

evidence.note: The export request returns 500 with error code export_failed, which is the primary failure.
The console logs the export failure with a 500 status.
The user is shown the "Export failed." message, confirming the failure is visible.

body.suspected_cause: A likely server-side error in the export endpoint, since it returns 500 with export_failed while the client request itself is sent normally.

body.title: QuickBooks 'Sync now' fails with 500 on /api/integrations/quickbooks/sync from Settings > Integrations
body.summary: The user opened the Integrations settings page and clicked Sync now for QuickBooks. The sync request returned a 500 (sync_failed) after 5100 ms, and the user saw a 'Sync failed' message.
body.expected: The QuickBooks sync runs and completes successfully without an error message.
body.actual: The POST to /api/integrations/quickbooks/sync returned 500 after 5100 ms with sync_failed, and the user saw 'Sync failed. We'll retry automatically.'

evidence.note: The sync request itself returned 500 (sync_failed) after 5100 ms, which is the primary failure.
The user was shown the sync failure message, confirming the error reached the UI.

body.suspected_cause: The likely cause is a server-side failure in the QuickBooks sync endpoint, possibly a timeout or upstream error given the 5100 ms response time before the 500.

body.title: Revenue report crashes with RangeError when applying a custom date range
body.summary: The user opened the revenue report and set a custom date range using the date picker, then clicked Apply. The page showed a generic error message instead of the report, and the user repeatedly clicked Apply without success.

steps_to_reproduce.text: Enter a start date in the date-from field.

body.expected: The report loads for the selected date range.
body.actual: The app throws a RangeError (Invalid time value) in formatDateRange and the page shows "Something went wrong loading this report." Repeated clicks on Apply do not recover it.

evidence.note: Primary failure: unhandled RangeError in formatDateRange at DateRangePicker.tsx:112.
User-visible error message shown instead of the report.
Six rapid clicks on Apply show the user retrying with no change.

body.suspected_cause: The date range formatter likely receives an unparseable or empty date value from the date-from input when Apply is clicked, causing an Invalid Date to be formatted.

body.title: Payments page crashes with 'Something went wrong' when Refunds filter is clicked (PaymentsTable formatRow null amount)
body.summary: The user opened the Payments page and clicked the Refunds filter. The table then failed with a TypeError reading 'amount' of null in formatRow, and the user saw 'Something went wrong.' Same signature as BUG-280 (closed); likely a regression.
body.expected: The Refunds filter applies and the payments list shows refund rows.
body.actual: A TypeError is thrown in formatRow (PaymentsTable.tsx:77:30) and the user sees 'Something went wrong.'

evidence.note: Primary failure: null is read for 'amount' in formatRow, which is the crash point.
The user-facing error message appears at the same moment the exception fires.

body.suspected_cause: A likely cause is that formatRow receives a null payment record for some refund rows and does not guard against a missing amount.
body.signature: exc:TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'amount') @ PaymentsTable.tsx
